part.text: Data is clean and highly linear. Let me check fit sensitivity (high-strain points), curvature, and whether the PNG device works.

input.content:
d <- read.csv("measurements.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# sensitivity: drop top 2 strain points per specimen
d2 <- d[d$strain <= 0.0016, ]
cat("Full-range vs trimmed (0.0002-0.0016) slopes:\n")
for (s in unique(d$specimen)) {
  m1 <- lm(stress_mpa ~ strain, data = d[d$specimen == s, ])
  m2 <- lm(stress_mpa ~ strain, data = d2[d2$specimen == s, ])
  cat(sprintf("%-6s full=%7.0f trimmed=%7.0f  diff=%+6.0f (%.1f%%)\n",
              s, coef(m1)[2], coef(m2)[2],
              coef(m2)[2] - coef(m1)[2], 100 * (coef(m2)[2] / coef(m1)[2] - 1)))
}

cat("\nQuadratic term test (p-value for strain^2, per material):\n")
for (mat in unique(d$material)) {
  sub <- d[d$material == mat, ]
  m <- lm(stress_mpa ~ strain + I(strain^2), data = sub)
  cat(sprintf("%-9s coef=%10.3g  p=%.4f\n", mat, coef(m)[3], summary(m)$coefficients[3, 4]))
}

cat("\nPooled fit per material (common slope, specimen intercepts):\n")
for (mat in unique(d$material)) {
  sub <- d[d$material == mat, ]
  m <- lm(stress_mpa ~ 0 + specimen + strain, data = sub)
  cf <- summary(m)$coefficients
  cat(sprintf("%-9s slope=%7.0f  se=%5.0f  R2=%.5f\n", mat, cf["strain", 1], cf["strain", 2], summary(m)$r.squared))
}

cat("\nMaterial summary (mean of specimen slopes):\n")
for (mat in unique(d$material)) {
  sl <- sapply(unique(d$specimen[d$material == mat]), function(s)
    coef(lm(stress_mpa ~ strain, data = d[d$specimen == s, ]))[2])
  cat(sprintf("%-9s mean=%7.0f  sd=%5.0f  se=%5.0f  cv=%.2f%%\n",
              mat, mean(sl), sd(sl), sd(sl) / sqrt(length(sl)), 100 * sd(sl) / mean(sl)))
}

cat("\nPNG device test: ")
png("/private/tmp/tmp8cuxtgpo/tmp/opencode/test.png", width = 600, height = 400, res = 120)
plot(1:10)
dev.off()
cat("ok\n")

part.text: The data are clean, linear (quadratic term p > 0.2 for all materials, R² ≥ 0.998), and a trimmed-range check changes slopes by <3%. Now I'll write the reproducible analysis script.

input.content:
# Elastic modulus from tensile stress-strain data
#
# Reads measurements.csv (specimen, material, strain, stress_mpa), fits
# stress = E * strain + b by ordinary least squares for each specimen, and
# summarises E per material. Writes:
#   modulus_summary.csv  - per-specimen and per-material fit results
#   modulus_fits.png     - data with fitted lines, one panel per material
#   results.md           - written separately (numbers below feed it)
#
# Usage (from the project directory):
#   Rscript analysis.R

d <- read.csv("measurements.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

## ---- validation ----------------------------------------------------------
stopifnot(
  identical(names(d), c("specimen", "material", "strain", "stress_mpa")),
  !anyNA(d),
  all(d$strain > 0),
  all(d$stress_mpa > 0)
)
if (any(duplicated(d[, c("specimen", "strain")]))) {
  stop("duplicated specimen/strain pairs")
}
# strain must increase with row order within each specimen
by_spec <- split(d, d$specimen)
for (s in names(by_spec)) {
  if (is.unsorted(by_spec[[s]]$strain)) stop("strain not increasing in ", s)
}
# each specimen belongs to exactly one material
if (any(tapply(d$material, d$specimen, function(x) length(unique(x))) != 1)) {
  stop("a specimen maps to more than one material")
}

materials <- unique(d$material)
specimens <- unique(d$specimen)

## ---- per-specimen fits ---------------------------------------------------
fit_one <- function(sub) {
  m <- lm(stress_mpa ~ strain, data = sub)
  cf <- summary(m)$coefficients
  data.frame(
    level         = "specimen",
    material      = sub$material[1],
    specimen      = sub$specimen[1],
    n_points      = nrow(sub),
    modulus_mpa   = unname(cf["strain", "Estimate"]),
    modulus_se_mpa = unname(cf["strain", "Std. Error"]),
    intercept_mpa = unname(cf["(Intercept)", "Estimate"]),
    r_squared     = summary(m)$r.squared,
    resid_sd_mpa  = summary(m)$sigma,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

spec_fits <- do.call(rbind, lapply(by_spec, fit_one))
rownames(spec_fits) <- NULL
spec_fits <- spec_fits[order(match(spec_fits$material, materials),
                             spec_fits$specimen), ]

## ---- per-material summary ------------------------------------------------
mat_fits <- do.call(rbind, lapply(materials, function(mat) {
  e <- spec_fits$modulus_mpa[spec_fits$material == mat]
  n <- length(e)
  data.frame(
    level          = "material",
    material       = mat,
    specimen       = NA_character_,
    n_points       = sum(spec_fits$n_points[spec_fits$material == mat]),
    modulus_mpa    = mean(e),
    modulus_se_mpa = sd(e) / sqrt(n),        # SE of the mean across specimens

input.content:
# Elastic modulus from tensile stress–strain data

## Summary

| Material | Specimens | E (GPa) | SD across specimens (GPa) | 95% CI (GPa) | R² range |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Aluminum | AL‑1, AL‑2, AL‑3 | **69.4** | 1.8 | ±4.4 | 0.9988–0.9995 |
| Steel | ST‑1, ST‑2, ST‑3 | **199.1** | 2.0 | ±5.0 | 0.9984–0.9988 |
| Titanium | TI‑1, TI‑2, TI‑3 | **116.6** | 1.7 | ±4.2 | 0.9978–0.9987 |

All three materials show an essentially linear stress–strain response over the tested range
(0.02 %–0.20 % strain), with R² ≥ 0.998 for every specimen. The measured moduli are consistent
with typical handbook values for aluminum alloys (~70 GPa), steel (~200 GPa) and titanium
alloys (~110–120 GPa).

![Stress–strain data with per-specimen linear fits](modulus_fits.png)

## Method

For each specimen, the elastic modulus was estimated by ordinary least squares from

$$\sigma = E\,\varepsilon + b$$

using all 10 data points (strain 0.0002–0.0020 in steps of 0.0002). The intercept \(b\) was
included to absorb any stress offset; it was not forced through zero. The reported material
modulus is the **mean of the three specimen slopes**, and the uncertainty is the
specimen-to-specimen standard deviation. The 95 % confidence interval is
\(t_{0.975,2}\,SD/\sqrt{3} = 4.303\,SD/\sqrt{3}\), reflecting the small number of replicates.

## Per-specimen results

| Specimen | E (GPa) | Fit SE (GPa) | Intercept (MPa) | R² |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| AL‑1 | 70.12 | 0.57 | −0.79 | 0.99947 |
| AL‑2 | 67.38 | 0.84 | 0.86 | 0.99876 |
| AL‑3 | 70.64 | 0.75 | −1.00 | 0.99911 |
| ST‑1 | 201.22 | 2.45 | −1.51 | 0.99882 |
| ST‑2 | 197.28 | 2.62 | 1.18 | 0.99859 |
| ST‑3 | 198.69 | 2.86 | 2.19 | 0.99835 |
| TI‑1 | 114.62 | 1.91 | −0.02 | 0.99778 |
| TI‑2 | 117.83 | 1.64 | −2.22 | 0.99845 |
| TI‑3 | 117.23 | 1.50 | −0.08 | 0.99869 |

Intercepts are all within ±2.2 MPa, i.e. at most ~0.5 % of the largest stress in the data, so
the fits pass close to the origin as expected in the elastic regime.

## Data quality and checks

- 90 rows, 9 specimens × 10 points; no missing values or duplicated specimen/strain pairs.
- Strain increases monotonically within every specimen and follows the same grid throughout.
- **Linearity:** adding a quadratic term does not improve the fit significantly for any material
  (p = 0.46 aluminum, 0.33 steel, 0.22 titanium). Residual scatter is small (1–5 MPa).
- **Range sensitivity:** refitting after dropping the two highest-strain points changes specimen
  moduli by at most 3.0 % (ST‑3); most change by <1.5 %. The result is therefore not sensitive
  to possible early stiffening near the proportional limit.
- **Scatter:** the fit standard error per specimen (0.6–2.9 GPa) is smaller than the
  specimen-to-specimen SD (1.7–2.0 GPa), so the uncertainty on each material modulus is dominated
  by specimen variability, not by the regression itself.

## Caveats

- Only three specimens per material, so the 95 % CI is wide; treat the single-decimal modulus as
  an estimate, not a precise material constant.
- The data stop at 0.2 % strain. This is enough for an elastic modulus but says nothing about
  yield strength, ductility or the proportional limit.
- Specimen IDs do not specify alloy/condition, so comparisons with handbook values are indicative
  only.

## Files

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `analysis.R` | Reproducible analysis (validation, fits, figure, CSV export) |
| `modulus_summary.csv` | Per-specimen and per-material fit statistics |
| `modulus_fits.png` | Data points and individual linear fits, one panel per material |
| `measurements.csv` | Input data (unchanged) |

Reproduce with:

```sh
Rscript analysis.R
```

3: ## Summary
4:

9: | Titanium | TI-1, TI-2, TI-3 | **116.6** | 1.7 | ±4.2 | 0.9978–0.9987 |
10: 
11: All three materials show an essentially linear stress–strain response over the tested range
12: (0.02 %–0.20 % strain), with R² ≥ 0.998 for every specimen. The measured moduli are consistent
13: with typical handbook values for aluminum alloys (~70 GPa), steel (~200 GPa) and titanium
14: alloys (~110–120 GPa).

16: ![Stress–strain data with per-specimen linear fits](modulus_fits.png)
17: 
18: ## Method
19: 
20: For each specimen, the elastic modulus was estimated by ordinary least squares from
21: 
22: ```text
23: stress = E * strain + b
24: ```
25: 
26: using all 10 data points (strain 0.0002–0.0020 in steps of 0.0002). The intercept `b` was
27: included to absorb any stress offset; it was not forced through zero. The reported material
28: modulus is the **mean of the three specimen slopes**, and the uncertainty is the
29: specimen-to-specimen standard deviation. The 95 % confidence interval is
30: `t(0.975, 2) * SD / sqrt(3) = 4.303 * SD / sqrt(3)`, reflecting the small number of replicates.
31: 
32: ## Per-specimen results
33: 
34: | Specimen | E (GPa) | Fit SE (GPa) | Intercept (MPa) | R² |
35: |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
36: | AL-1 | 70.12 | 0.57 | −0.79 | 0.99947 |
37: | AL-2 | 67.38 | 0.84 | 0.86 | 0.99876 |
38: | AL-3 | 70.64 | 0.75 | −1.00 | 0.99911 |
39: | ST-1 | 201.22 | 2.45 | −1.51 | 0.99882 |
40: | ST-2 | 197.28 | 2.62 | 1.18 | 0.99859 |
41: | ST-3 | 198.69 | 2.86 | 2.19 | 0.99835 |
42: | TI-1 | 114.62 | 1.91 | −0.02 | 0.99778 |

50: 
51: - 90 rows, 9 specimens × 10 points; no missing values or duplicated specimen/strain pairs.
52: - Strain increases monotonically within every specimen and follows the same grid throughout.

54:   (p = 0.46 aluminum, 0.33 steel, 0.22 titanium). Residual scatter is small (1–5 MPa).

69:   only.

part.text:
Done. Analysis is in place and reproducible with `Rscript analysis.R`.

**Elastic moduli (mean of 3 specimens ± SD):**

| Material | E (GPa) | R² |
|---|---:|---:|
| Aluminum | 69.4 ± 1.8 | 0.9988–0.9995 |
| Steel | 199.1 ± 2.0 | 0.9984–0.9988 |
| Titanium | 116.6 ± 1.7 | 0.9978–0.9987 |

**Files created:**
- `results.md` — write-up with method, per-specimen table, quality checks and caveats
- `modulus_fits.png` — data points plus individual fits in one panel per material
- `modulus_summary.csv` — per-specimen and per-material fit statistics (E, SE, R², intercept, CIs)
- `analysis.R` — validation, fits, figure and CSV export

**Notes:** The data are clean (90 points, no missing/duplicate entries), and the whole 0.02–0.20 % strain range behaves linearly — a quadratic term is not significant (p = 0.22–0.46), and dropping the two highest-strain points changes the slopes by at most 3 %. Intercepts are within ±2.2 MPa, so the fits pass essentially through the origin. With only three specimens per material, the 95% CIs are fairly wide (±4–5 GPa), and the scatter between specimens dominates the regression uncertainty. The measured values fall in the expected handbook ranges for these materials.
